Definition: perhaps from G4078 (through the idea of piercing); sharp (pungent), i.e. acrid (literally or figuratively):--bitter.
BiblicalUsage: Pikros means bitter, sharp to the taste. James asks whether a fountain sends forth sweet water and bitter from the same place in James 3:11, and warns against bitter envying and strife in the heart in James 3:14.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe one spring cannot give two kinds of water, and my mouth tells the truth about my heart.
